title: Rogers–Ramanujan bijections: verify the gap and plan one exact target
objective: Produce a source-audited, separately criticized plan for one genuinely unresolved constructive partition-bijection target from the historical brief, or document why no defensible target has been selected; do not execute or claim a proof in this initial increment.
deliverables: A dated primary-source status table separating count identities, bijections, stronger map properties and formalizations
At most two precise candidate statements and one recommended target, or a documented selection blocker
An explicit map class, proof-obligation DAG, smallest falsifiers and bounded enumeration protocol
An inventory-based Lean and dependency plan with final semantic and formal acceptance gates
Separate critic findings based on re-inspection of the selected gap's primary sources, author revisions, unresolved disagreements and a reviewable implementation plan
success_criteria: Historical status claims are re-audited or explicitly unverified; no known result is silently substituted for the intended open contribution
The proposed target fixes every partition restriction, parameter, quantifier, weight and claimed statistic, and compares the intended construction with the closest known maps
Forward/inverse well-definedness, weight preservation, termination and both inverse identities have explicit proof obligations and falsifiers
The plan respects role separation, two bounded rounds and the dispatch limit, while reporting excluded resources separately
The output is labeled as a plan; no unexecuted worker call, finite check or Lean build is reported as completed research
stop_conditions: After two proposal/challenge/revision rounds, preserve blockers and disagreements rather than start another round
Required primary sources cannot be inspected: mark status unverified and identify the missing evidence
The purported gap is already covered by an existing construction: attribute it and return alternatives for the user rather than silently expand scope
A candidate's refined counts or map constraints fail: retain the smallest counterexample and narrow or reject the proposal
This planning increment does not authorize proof execution, new dependency provisioning, paid adapters or publication
